title: Intelligent Runtime Safety Monitoring for Trustworthy Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems
content: Autonomous Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) are increasingly being adopted in autonomous vehicles, robotic coordination, smart manufacturing, healthcare, cybersecurity, and intelligent decision-support applications. Although multiple autonomous agents can independently plan, communicate, and act, their interactions introduce system-level safety risks in which incorrect actions, unreliable agents, corrupted communication, or changing environmental conditions can propagate across the system. Existing approaches often focus on pre-deployment verification or address individual concerns such as trust, communication security, or policy verification. This paper presents an Intelligent Runtime Safety Monitoring framework for trustworthy autonomous multi-agent systems that continuously observes agent states, actions, communications, and decisions during execution. The proposed framework integrates formal safety verification, risk assessment, dynamic trust estimation, explainable decision-making, and adaptive self-correction. Based on the detected safety condition, the framework can allow, warn, block, re-plan, isolate, or escalate an event for human intervention. For empirical evaluation, the study adopts public autonomous-driving motion resources, using the nuScenes dataset as the primary pilot resource and the Waymo Open Motion Dataset as a scale-up benchmark. The proposed methodology defines data preprocessing, safety-event construction, baseline comparisons, evaluation metrics, statistical analysis, and visualization procedures. The paper intentionally distinguishes dataset-grounded analysis from empirical performance claims, as completed benchmark results are not yet available in the current study. The framework provides a modular foundation for improving runtime safety, reliability, explainability, and adaptive response in autonomous multi-agent systems.
